input.subject: Kitchen socket – safety steps for now
input.body:
Job Id: NBL-020-01
Address: 8 Brindlewick Row, Oakhollow, ZZ1 1ZZ

Hi Nora,

Thank you for the update, and sorry you have not had safety advice from us before now. Until a qualified electrician has checked it, please follow these steps:

Do not use the socket, plug anything into it or touch the socket face.

If you can see a breaker at the consumer unit clearly labelled for the kitchen sockets, and you can reach it with dry hands without touching the socket, please switch that breaker off. This may also switch off the fridge, so keep the fridge door closed as much as possible. If the breakers are not labelled or you are unsure, do not open or work on the unit; leave it and tell us.

If the smell gets stronger, or you see smoke, sparks, scorch marks, hear crackling, or a smoke alarm sounds, leave the property with your son straight away and call 999.

We have gone back to your landlord this evening asking him to authorise a qualified electrician, and our duty manager is dealing with this now. We will update you as soon as we have a decision. Please reply here and tell us whether you were able to switch off a breaker.

Kind regards
Northbridge Lettings

A warm socket with a burning smell is a possible fire risk, so we strongly recommend that a qualified electrician attends as soon as possible to make the socket safe and test it, and quotes for anything more than making safe. Can you please confirm by reply straight away that you are happy for us to instruct a qualified electrician for this, or tell us which qualified electrician you would like to send instead. Kind regards
Northbridge Lettings
